newsitem.title: USA: Alza buys Bayer treatment for AIDS infection.
newsitem.headline: Alza buys Bayer treatment for AIDS infection.

text.p: Alza Corp. said Tuesday it has acquired a treatment for a common AIDS infection from Bayer AG for a $50 million upfront payment plus possible royalties.
Under the deal, Bayer will manufacture the product, Mycelex Troche, for Alza, which will make payments based on net sales.

Mycelex Troche is a slow-dissolving lozenge for the treatment and prevention of oropharyngeal candidiasis, a painful infection also known as oral thrush. The infection is prevalent in AIDS patients and others with compromised immune systems, such as those receiving chemotherapy.
Alza, based in Palo Alto, Calif., develops pharmaceutical products using advanced drug delivery technologies.
Bayer is a research-based German company with major businesses in health care, chemicals and imaging technologies. It had 1996 sales of $9 billion and employs 23,500 people.
Alza's stock edged up 6 cents to $29.06 on the New York Stock Exchange at midafternoon.
